question: For a Aerospace / Defense use case involving radar, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?
answer: The Vault contains no test workflow that places a Signaling / Non-signaling Tester inside a radar test chain. Radar in this Vault appears in two unrelated places: as an instrument category, the R&S AREG800A "Automotive Radar Echo Generator" for dynamic artificial object generation (automotive, not aerospace/defense radar), and as a Counter-UAV detection sensor category ("Radar Systems" to track drones over long ranges), which the Vault records only as a source listing without band, RCS, method, or products. Where the Vault does position signaling and non-signaling testers is the 5G device testing value chain: Signaling / protocol / application maps to R&S CMX500 / CMW500 / CMsquares, while Production / manufacturing maps to R&S CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 (the CMP180 is described as a "production / R&D non-signaling tester"). In aerospace/defense-adjacent material the signaling tester sits on the communications-link side, not the radar sensor side: the CMX500 is used as the 5G network emulator in the deployed private-5G / smart-jamming (A&D) test setup, and in the UAV signaling test solution it covers LTE / 5G / Wi-Fi link signaling plus multi-technology de-sense validation. The Vault explicitly forbids crossing these domains, stating that a CMX500 signaling option must not be inferred as an EMC/EME test system, nor an EMC system inferred as a cellular / WLAN protocol tester. Military drone/aviation testing in the Vault is covered by EMC / EME standards (MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-464, RTCA DO-160) and EMI/EMS systems, not by signaling testers. So the only defensible placement is: a signaling/non-signaling tester belongs to the radio-communication-link and production-RF stages of a radar-platform program (and to de-sense / coexistence validation between the radar and the comms links), while radar echo/target simulation and EME testing are handled by different instruments.
missing: No Vault page describes an aerospace/defense radar test workflow (radar TX/RX characterization, pulse/chirp analysis, target/echo simulation, EW threat emulation) with ordered test stages, and none places a Signaling / Non-signaling Tester in such a workflow. Missing: any A&D radar test plan or stage sequence; any statement linking CMX500/CMP180-class testers to radar measurement; radar bands/RCS/waveform or MIL-STD radar test methods; and whether the AREG800A (documented only as automotive) is offered for aerospace/defense radar at all.

key_points.point: The Vault's radar-specific instrument is the AREG800A automotive radar echo generator, not a signaling tester.

key_points.point: Radar in the Vault's defense/counter-UAV context is only a detection sensor category with no test method or product detail.

key_points.point: In the device testing value chain, signaling testers (CMX500/CMW500) occupy the signaling / protocol / application layer.

key_points.point: Non-signaling testers (CMP180/CMP200/CMW100) are mapped to the production / manufacturing stage.
